---
description: Write or update a spec using the speckit 4-part recipe
---

# speckit.specify

The student is about to describe something they want built. Your job is to capture it as
a spec — BEFORE any code.

## Steps

1. Read `speckit/constitution.md` and `speckit/spec-template.md`.
2. From the student's request (and the cheat-sheet prompts in `docs/04-cheat-sheet.md` if
   they point at one), write `speckit/station-specs/<name>-spec.md` with exactly four
   sections: What it is / What it looks like / What it must do / What to leave out.
3. The "must do" items MUST be checkable statements (a checkbox you could tick by looking
   at the screen or the chain).
4. Show the student the finished spec and ask them to confirm or edit one line of it.
   Confirmation is the phase gate. Do not proceed to plan yet.
5. If the request violates `speckit/constitution.md` (keys, mainnet, real money), correct
   the spec toward the constitution and say why.

Keep the spec under ~40 lines. Plain language, no jargon without a one-line gloss.
